The ledgers of the `gcal` fixture with `slack` settings instead of `cal`: `primary` (weekly, midnight boundaries) names `team heads-up`, `secondary` (09:00 boundaries) names `second`. `slack.csv` holds three presets and one id row: `team` posts the default text to `#oncall-team` at the handover and keeps `@oncall`; `heads-up` sends a reminder to `{who}` three days before the shift start (`when=-3d`); `second` posts to the channel id `C0SECOND` and keeps the same `@oncall`; `alice | id | U0ALICE` is a cached id that parsing leaves alone. At `now` 2026-10-05T10:00 the shift of the moment is dave@example.com's 10-05 shift for every preset (the heads-up window `[10-02, 10-09)` contains `now` too). `slack-state.csv` already records the channel messages of `primary/team` and `secondary/second` for the current shifts, so only the heads-up to dave@example.com is due (`expected/slack.json`; `{prev}` is carol, `{next}` is empty because the pinned 10-12 shift has nobody); its two other rows name a rotation (`tertiary`) and a preset (`old`) that no longer exist and are dropped from the state rows a post would write (`expected/slack-state.csv`, the new row stamped with `now`). `@oncall` unions both rotations: dave@example.com and frank. The golden run (`golden.test.js`) loads the Slack extension because the directory holds a `slack.csv` and shows the plan in a `Slack (no slack)` block of `expected/status.txt`.
